label: Today You Will Learn
h: How to separate what you feel from what you choose, and how to hear the sentences that turn anxiety into shame.
body: About 8 minutes, plus one short pause · one small practice · no homework list

label: Key Scripture
h: "When I am afraid, I put my trust in you."

label: Name The Problem
h:
Anxiety is one burden.
Shame about anxiety is a second.

label: The Main Truth
h:
Fear is an experience.
Trust is a direction.
body:
feartrust

Fear and trust can live in the same prayer at the same time.

label: The Tool · Four Things That Are Not The Same
body:
A feelingFear, dread, worry. It arrives; you did not summon it.
A body reactionRacing heart, tight chest, no sleep. Not a moral act.
An unwanted thought"God has left me." Arriving is not agreeing.
A chosen responseWhat you do next. This is where trust lives.

label: The Sentences That Turn Anxiety Into Shame
body:
"If I trusted God, I would not feel this way."

"I should be able to pray this away."

"A real Christian should not be anxious."

Each one judges a feeling as if it were a choice.

label: But Doesn'T The Bible Say "Do Not Be Anxious"?
h: Paul does not say "so stop." He says "so pray."
body: Instruction is not condemnation. It points you in a direction; it does not pass judgement on every feeling that has not yet followed.

label: Do This Now
h: Write one sentence you have told yourself about your faith because of anxiety.
body:
Then rewrite it truthfully. For example: "I feel afraid, and I am choosing to trust God with it."

Pause the audio

label: Remember
h: Your faith does not live in your pulse.

label: Prayer
body:
Father, when I am afraid,
I put my trust in you.

Take the shame I have added to my fear.

You do not condemn me.
Teach me not to condemn myself.

Amen.
